verdict: Visa's net revenue jumped 17% to $11.2B — its fastest growth since 2022 — and profit rose 32% to $6.0B, helped by last year's far bigger litigation bill not repeating.

segments.name: Service revenue
segments.note: Fees from banks for using the Visa brand and network on cards.

segments.name: Data processing revenue
segments.note: Fees for clearing and processing each transaction — processed transactions grew 9%.

segments.name: International transaction revenue
segments.note: Fees when a card is used outside its home country — cross-border volume rose 12%.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Value-added services — fraud tools, data and consulting for banks and merchants.

opex.name: Personnel
opex.note: Pay and benefits for Visa's workforce.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day.

opex.name: Litigation provision
opex.note: Mostly the interchange multidistrict litigation (MDL) case — a legal charge Visa excludes from its non-GAAP results.

opex.name: Network, professional & depreciation
opex.note: Network and processing ($260M), professional fees ($238M) and depreciation & amortization ($333M).

follow100Note: Per $100 of gross revenue (before client incentives). Measured against Visa's reported net revenue of $11.2B instead, the kept profit is $53.62 per $100. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Fastest growth since 2022
takeaways.text: Net revenue rose 17% to $11.2B — data processing +18%, service revenue +13%, international transactions +10% on cross-border volume +12%, and other revenue +41%. Payments volume grew 9% and processed transactions 9%.

takeaways.title: EPS jumped 36%
takeaways.text: GAAP EPS rose 36% to $3.14, largely because the litigation provision fell to $329M from $1,000M a year ago. Non-GAAP EPS, which strips out the legal charge and other one-offs, was $3.31, up 20%.

takeaways.title: Incentives keep climbing
takeaways.text: Client incentives — rebates paid to issuing banks and partners — rose 14% to $4.2B, about 27 cents of every gross revenue dollar. They grow fast because the biggest banks negotiate hard to stay on the network.

oneTimers: A litigation provision of $329M sits in operating expenses; $311M of it is the special item for the interchange multidistrict litigation (MDL) case and other legal matters (a year ago the special item was $992M). Visa excludes it from non-GAAP results.

Also excluded from non-GAAP results: $86M of amortization of acquired intangible assets and acquisition-related costs, and $15M of net losses on equity investments. Non-GAAP net income was $6.3B ($3.31 per share).
otherDetail: Investment income and other gains of $118M, less $178M of interest expense — net -$60M.
footerNote: Visa reports 'net revenue' of $11,230M; this page starts from gross revenue of $15,475M so the $4,245M of client incentives shows as a cost.
